content.title: Compare 5-year ARM Mortgage Rates
content.text: Today's 5-year ARM rates | Wednesday, April 22, 2026Last updated 1:40 PM EDTOn Wednesday afternoon, April 22, 2026, the average interest rate on a 5-year adjustable-rate mortgage fell one basis point to 6.39% APR, compared to yesterday.The 5-year ARM rate is four basis points higher than one week ago and 81 basis points lower than one year ago.A basis point is one hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%. We describe mortgage rates’ ups and downs in basis points because they simplify comparisons.NerdWallet’s rates are expressed as an annual percentage rate, or APR, and our mortgage rates data comes from Zillow.What to Know About 5-year ARM Mortgage Rates Shop and compare today's 5-year ARM rates in the table above. +1+2Written by Holden Lewis, Reviewed by Michelle Blackford, Edited by Mary MakarushkaWritten by Holden Lewis and Last updated 04/22/2026What is a 5-year ARM?A 5-year ARM is an adjustable-rate mortgage with an interest rate that stays the same for the first five years. After that initial period, the rate adjusts periodically based on changes in the broader market.A 5-year ARM typically begins with a lower introductory rate than a fixed-rate loan has. After the five years are over, the rate can adjust up or down every six months. The rate adjustments are based on a benchmark index, which in most cases is the secured overnight financing rate (SOFR), plus a fixed margin set by the lender. The benchmark rate tends to rise when the economy is strong and fall when the economy weakens.Different lenders may refer to the 5-year ARM by different names. It's sometimes called the 5/6 ARM, where the "5" refers to the starting fixed-rate period in years and the "6" refers to how often in months the rate is adjusted afterward. The 5/6 ARM is the most popular type of ARM available today. NerdWallet’s mortgage comparison tool can help you find competitive 5-year ARM rates today, whether you’re buying a home or refinancing. At the top of this page, enter details about the loan you’re looking for and click “See rates” to get rate quotes without providing personal information.When to consider a 5-year ARMA 5-year ARM makes sense if you expect to refinance your mortgage or sell your house before the introductory rate expires. You may be able to qualify for a larger loan because of the ARM's low introductory rate. Note that the interest rate and monthly payment could climb substantially if the index rate rises anytime after the first five years are up.ARM glossaryIndex: The benchmark rate that reflects overall market conditions. Most ARMs use the 30-day average SOFR (SOFR), which can rise or fall over time. The index is used together with the margin to determine your adjustable interest rate. Margin: A fixed number of percentage points that the lender adds to the index to calculate the interest rate at each adjustment. The margin does not change over the life of the loan. For example, if the index rate is 3.985% and your margin is 2.75 percentage points, your interest rate would be 6.75% after rounding. Rate cap: The maximum amount your loan’s interest rate can increase or decrease at the first adjustment, each time thereafter and over the life of the loan. Rate caps help protect borrowers from large, sudden payment changes.Learn more about adjustable-rate mortgages
